purpose: Directional blind check of the generic C-route readability-floor change against the frozen A renders. This small holdout is not a replacement for the frozen 20-comparison blind study and cannot switch the shipped default.

reviewer.promptContract: Return a two-slot ranking based only on visible narrative clarity, hierarchy, presentation-scale typography, composition variety, information relationships, spacing, and rendering defects. Do not infer provenance or reward slide count.

comparisons.notes: C had clearer presentation-scale typography, stronger hierarchy, more varied compositions, and easier-to-follow visual relationships; A was more repetitive and denser.
C had stronger typography, clearer hierarchy, more varied compositions, and more legible relationships; A was sparse with undersized labels and repeated white layouts.

C had stronger presentation-scale legibility, bolder hierarchy, clearer visual relationships, and more varied compositions; A was polished but its serif copy and labels were smaller and its layouts sparser.

C had substantially stronger typography, clearer hierarchy, varied compositions, and cleaner relationships between question, method, result, robustness, interpretation, and limitation; A was denser and more repetitive.

summary.interpretation: All four directional comparisons favored the updated C render. The result is consistent with the readability-floor hypothesis but is too small to replace the frozen blind score or establish the 60% default-switch threshold.
